newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index drops 1.03pts in listless trading.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index drops 1.03pts in listless trading.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mixed in listless trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, with losses to VUB bank driving the SAX index down 1.03 to 212.94 points.

Slovakia's largest commercial bank VUB lost 100 crowns to close at 1,850, with its average price -- used in calculating the index -- easing 2.79 percent and accounting for the major part of the SAX's drop.
"It seems that financial institutions, together with VUB and IRB Bank, are slowly falling back to their previous price levels," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt.
Oil refiner Slovnaft, the most capitalised issue on the floor, closed unchanged at 950 crowns, but brokers said its average price fell 0.53 percent, also contributing to the drop of the index.
"Slovnaft shares are trading in low volumes at the current price, as larger packages are only available for about 1,000 crowns," Briska said.
The only two blue chips to post moderate gains were oil and gas storage company Nafta and steel producer VSZ. Nafta closed up 50 at 2,050 crowns, while VSZ gained 16 to close at 658.
Brokers said Nafta's price was higher due to block trades with larger packages of shares, and they expected the price to hover around its current level for next few days.
VSZ remains one of the most stable issues on the floor and it price is not seen oscilating beyond the range of normal corrections.
Overall volume increased to 178,583 shares traded from 92,569 shares on Wednesday, while turnover rose to 249.49 million crowns from 83.99 million.
